Main conclusion

Document structure is useful for focus and early precision, but forcing retrieval through one section can hide relevant evidence. The strongest next design is hybrid: index-guided routing with a small global fallback.

Experiment methodology

A controlled comparison inspired by IBM Research's STAIR paper.

Flat RAG

Question → all chunks → answer

Dense similarity search runs over all 395 overlapping passages. This maximizes the opportunity to recover evidence from anywhere in the report.

→
Index-guided RAG

Question → section → chunks → answer

The system first chooses one of 54 authored sections, then retrieves passages only from that section. This narrows the evidence but creates a routing dependency.

Controlled variables

Same sourceWorld Development Report 2024.
Same embedding modelBAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5.
Same answer generation setupIdentical prompt, model, and retrieved-passage budget.
Changed variableThe retrieval layout: global passage search or section-first routing.

How to read the metrics

Hit@1, Hit@3, Hit@5The share of questions where a gold section appears within the first 1, 3, or 5 results.
MRRMean reciprocal rank. It rewards placing the first relevant result near the top.
Manual quality scoreAverage rating across correctness, grounding, completeness, and citation quality.

Relationship to the paper

STAIR predicts a relevant leaf section from a question and a full table of contents, and evaluates on the SearchTome benchmark. AutoSTAIR does not reproduce that training setup. It benchmarks two practical RAG layouts over one public report, uses its existing authored structure, and evaluates both retrieval and final answers.
